title: Asked by parda: Forest: what prototyping found (layouts tried, why Flat exists, the API parda calls)
body:
Forest: what prototyping found (layouts tried, why Flat exists, the API parda calls) (graft:01a10a6b-bd3e..2a25, from parda)

What was needed:
- parda: Details for graft 01a10a64-df76 (sylva / Structures / Forest), from building and measuring crates/sylva-forest in parda2D (commit 7912896). All numbers: divan, a tree with 16 children per node numbered breadth first, 10k and 100k nodes, against a hand-written arena with a child Vec per node; the machine was sometimes loaded, so compare within one run and run twice (swings of 30% between runs happened).

(1) Link layout, measured: (a) one 20-byte record per node (parent, first, last, prev, next) with generation and alive in separate arrays: build 106 us at 10k, link-following preorder 13.4 us (arena 8.7). (b) Packing generation and alive into the record (28 bytes): link walks got slower, 17.6 us: more bytes dragged through cache per step. (c) One array per link field: build 168 us (twice as slow: five scattered writes per insert) and link walks 23 us. Kept (a).

(2) Why Flat: walking by links is latency-bound (each step waits for the previous load), so no link layout reaches the arena, whose stack hands it already-loaded indices. A preorder array (every live slot in preorder) makes full passes about 14x faster than the arena (0.66 vs 9.1 us at 10k). But a skipping walk over the preorder array with subtree ends (jump to end on skip) was 30-50% slower than the arena (2.6 vs 1.6 us), because every skip lands hundreds of entries ahead: a cache miss. Interleaving (slot, end) pairs didn't help. Contiguous child lists (CSR: all children in one array, each slot's range) fixed it: the siblings a walk checks share cache lines; now equal or faster (1.57 vs 1.64 us, 15.8 vs 16.6 us). So Flat keeps both: the preorder array for full passes, the child lists for skipping walks (with a reusable stack, hence walk(&mut self)).

(3) Flat::update rebuilds everything when Forest::version changed: 42 us at 10k, 422 us at 100k (preorder by links, subtree sizes in reverse preorder, child lists). Fine for parda (structure changes after reconciliation, not on animation frames); an incremental patch of only the changed subtree's range would cut it later.

(4) The build gap (about 10% at 100k, 1.1-2x at 10k with noisy medians): allocate pushes to three Vecs (links, generation, alive) and link() writes neighbours. Ideas not yet tried: links and generation in one record now that walks use Flat (walk speed no longer depends on the record size), a bulk append_children(parent, n) for reconciliation inserting rows, and skipping the Option<Id> rebuild in push_child.

(5) The API parda will call: Forest::new/with_capacity, push_root, push_child, insert_before, move_to(id, parent, before) with its errors (into its own subtree; before isn't a child), remove(id, |id| ...) with children before parents, contains, parent, first_child, last_child, next_sibling, prev_sibling, children, ancestors, roots, preorder, postorder, walk(root, visit -> Visit::Enter/Skip), version, slots, id_at(slot), Id::slot; Flat::new, update(&forest) -> bool, slots(), ends(), children_of(slot), walk(&mut self, visit); Column<T>::new, fit(&forest), get, get_mut, as_slice, as_mut_slice; Forest::to_tree(key, data) into sylva::tree::Tree. Keeping these names and semantics lets parda swap its dependency without code changes.

(6) A helper parda would use, not in the prototype: propagate a flag column to ancestors (mark a node and every ancestor dirty-below, stopping at the first already-marked one: O(depth) once per dirty node, O(1) amortized), since every incremental pass needs it.

(7) Smaller: generations are u32 and wrap (4 billion reuses of one slot before a stale id could match again: acceptable, worth a doc line); bytes per node today are 20 (links) + 4 (generation) + 1 (alive) plus Flat's 4 + 4 + 8 (slot, end, child range) + 4 per child entry.

Answer (done): Landed in sylva 938824e as sylva::forest, from your crates/sylva-forest, with your tests and benchmarks; what you measured is in DESIGN.md 3.4 and 6 and in the Forest node's journal. (5) Every name you listed is there with its semantics, with one difference: move_to returns Result<bool>, false (and no version bump, so no Flat rebuild) when the node is already where it was asked to go; `?;` and `.unwrap();` call sites compile unchanged. Also added: insert_after. Internally alive is gone: a slot's generation is even while alive, odd while free. (6) Forest::mark_with_ancestors(id, &mut Column<bool>) marks a node and its ancestors, stopping at the first one already marked. (7) The wrap is documented on Id (2^31 reuses of a slot, since parity takes a bit). (3) and (4) are todos on the node: patching Flat incrementally, and a bulk append_children; the 100k build gap measures 3-10% here, reordering children 12 vs 4 ns. You can switch your dependency to sylva::forest now.
